previousHostControl.note: The same bundle runs on the host that registers no NativeMicrotasksCxx: queueMicrotask has nothing to reach, so React's first update throws and the root does not mount. It fails exactly the checks that need the new module, and holds the three that need only the JS the bundle runs (the flag, and the global installed before the renderer reads it) and the lifecycle and report checks. Its native producers are pinned for the tree; the old binary was built from executionBaseCommit.

retainedSabotage.mechanism: flag-unset, promise-shim and gate-removed are in-memory esbuild overrides of src/runtime.js (scripts/react-microtasks-bundle.mjs), no file is edited; no-module breaks one line of native/application_runtime.cpp, rebuilds the host, keeps it in the variant's hostDirectory and restores the source byte for byte (scripts/sabotage-sources.mjs)

retainedSabotage.flagUnsetMatchesModel: The flag-unset lane comes out, case by case, in the order the oracle's model gives for the flag off (modelOrders.off), which says the model describes this host in the direction the passing lane does not show.

oracle.independence: Written from RN's pinned sources, not from the probe: setUpTimers' flag and where it installs queueMicrotask from, the spec and C++ of the NativeMicrotasks module, the renderer's flag branch (supportsMicrotasks, scheduleMicrotask, scheduleImmediateRootScheduleTask and the job it queues, read from ReactFabric-prod.js by the structure of its code), how a touch end becomes a discrete update, and the RuntimeScheduler's priority timeouts, checkpoint and ordering are read from the files; the order of each case is derived by a model of the host's event loop whose microtask queue is V8's own (Promise reactions, queueMicrotask and RN's immediateShim run in a vm context) and in which React's job goes where the flag branch puts it; every verdict of the probe is derived again from the report's raw observations.

limits: The cases are the handler of a Pressable's onPress in one headless root; the order of the commit relative to other work is certified for sync-lane updates of a discrete event, not for every lane.
The timer cases depend on the host taking a timer registered in a handler in a later pump than the RuntimeScheduler's loop; the oracle reads that order from native/application_runtime.cpp.
The gate is the host's extension (V2-D27); callback exceptions and a Promise storm are slice F's.
The registry counts the calls that reach RN's module in front of RN's own invoker; the module's C++ is compiled unchanged.
The headless desktop host only; no mobile export has run this bundle.
Hosted CI is pending: the record is of the local run.
